newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE SAYS TURKISH LIMIT IN AEGEAN OPERATIONS POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: GREECE SAYS TURKISH LIMIT IN AEGEAN OPERATIONS POSITIVE.

text.p: Greece said on Wednesday a Turkish decision to limit military activity in the Aegean Sea was a positive move already practiced by Athens to reduce tension between the two nervous NATO neighbours.

"They say they would respect international rules and that their planes would not be armed (over the Aegean) which is positive. We'll wait and see whether the Turkish side means what it says," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
"We will avoid military activity in the Aegean but we will be on the alert to intercept any violations (of Greek airspace and waters) by Turkey," he said.
Turkey's armed forces said on Tuesday they would temporarily limit activity in the Aegean Sea to support NATO-led measures to reduce tension with Greece.

"The Turkish navy and air force will carry out routine training and reconnaissance activities in the Aegean between July 1 and August 15 but there will be no manoeuvres during the period," military headquarters said in a statement.
Reppas said that Greece had already made a proposal for the moratorium to be extended to September 15 but Ankara had yet to respond positively.

The Turkish military said the move was being made "to support the intiative of NATO General Secretary (Javier) Solana, who has made great efforts on measures to reduce tension in the Aegean and build confidence."
The military said Turkish aircraft would not be armed when operating over the Aegean.
Turkey and Greece often carry out war games in the Aegean and last came close to war in January, 1996 over rights to a deserted islet close to the Turkish coast.
The historical rivals are also at odds over the divided Mediterranean island of Cyprus.
